data.narrative:
Phaidra is a Series B AI & Software company founded by former DeepMind leaders (CEO Jim Gao led Google's data center cooling AI project; lead engineer Vedavyas Panneershelvam contributed to AlphaGo). The company has raised $120M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 9 private AI & Software businesses at Series B stage and 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $120M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $228M. Peer-median analysis references three same-stage, same-sector comparables: Scale AI at $29.0B, Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, and Black Forest Labs at $3.2B. The median of these three is $5.6B, reflecting substantial valuation dispersion across the cohort.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $194M (low) to $6.4B (high), with a median of $2.9B. The stage-progression method anchors the low end, while peer multiples drive the upper bound. The wide range reflects tension between Phaidra's early-stage capital deployment ($120M raised) and the substantial valuations commanded by AI peers with comparable or less mature operating history. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to comparables, the sustainability of AI software valuations in a market correction, and whether Phaidra's industrial AI focus commands a valuation premium or discount relative to the broader peer set.
